Staging (test builds): vault release log

Staging release 27 (test build)

Release 27 stops vote message sizes from hinting at your choice, keeps vote records until their results check out, and lets desktops and agents name sessions.

Status

Status
Active
Published
2026-11-04
End date
Not set

The current release. New vaults are enrolled into it, and the app offers it to everyone on an older release.

Changes

  • Votes: the messages your vault sends about your vote, to the service and to your phone, are now the same size whatever you chose, so their size no longer hints at your choice.
  • Votes: if a vote's published results never check out, your vault now keeps its record as a problem until a later check succeeds or you release it. Before, a service could withhold its results for 7 days and then send enough new votes to push the record out.
  • Votes: a results check that gave up can now be checked again. If the results are later published and check out, the vote is settled with nothing for you to do. You get one notice when a check gives up, and it asks nothing of you.
  • Votes: the record of a vote you did not cast is now kept until its results check out, since that check is what shows that no one voted in your name. Before, it could be cleared away to make room before the check was even due.
  • Votes: your vault no longer clears away records of finished votes when a service is at its limit of open votes, and a vote it is still checking before showing it no longer counts toward that limit.
  • Votes: the notice that a service has too many votes with problems now goes away once it has fewer than 16, also when a late check clears one, not only when you release one.
  • Votes: if the published results list your vote's code twice, your vault now marks the results check as failed and keeps the extra rows as evidence, since a second row could hide a ballot in your name.
  • Votes: if your phone cannot get your own row of the published results, your vault now keeps the vote as a problem until a later check finds the row, and tells you once.
  • Votes: your vault now refuses a vote meant for more than 100,000 voters, whose published results would be too large for your phone to check.
  • Your vault now refuses a message containing a broken character code in its text, instead of quietly replacing the character. Correctly formed messages never contain one.
  • A desktop or agent ending its access can now name the session it means. If that session has already ended, expired or been replaced, your vault changes nothing: a newer session stays open, requests waiting for your approval stay, and nothing is added to your History.
  • So a late "end" from an earlier session can no longer end the one you just approved. Desktops and agents do not name their session yet. Ending access from your phone, including "Deny and end access now", is unchanged: it ends whatever access that device has.
  • A desktop or agent can now ask your vault for its own current session and when it expires. It never sees another device's session.
  • Your vault now gives your phone the other side's key with a connection request you sent, so the app can show its fingerprint before you approve. The apps do not show it yet.
  • If your vault were ever moved back to an older release, vote message sizes could again hint at your choice, vote records could be cleared before their results check out, a code listed twice in the results would go unnoticed, and desktops and agents could not name a session.
  • Time scale: 1 day = 1 hour (staging)
  • Built from vettid-vault commit 569746d (tag release/staging/27) and independently rebuilt on 2026-11-04 with a matching PCR0.

Security

Security fix: update recommended

Release 27 fixes three weaknesses in voting. The size of some messages your vault sent about a vote could depend on the choice you picked, so VettID's relay, which sees only the size of each message, could in some cases have told choices apart. A service could make your vault clear away a vote's record before its published results had checked out: by withholding them for 7 days, or, for a vote you did not cast, before the check was due. And your vault did not look for published results that list your vote's code twice. In either of the last two cases, a ballot the service had added or changed in your name could have gone unnoticed. We know of no use of any of them against any vault. Your PIN and credential password were not exposed. Vaults on releases 25 and 26 are affected.
